definition: The New Moon occurs when the Sun and Moon are aligned (0 degrees apart) — the Moon is invisible from Earth, marking the start of the roughly 29.5-day lunar cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Across many traditions the New Moon marked the start of the lunar month and was treated as an auspicious time for new beginnings, planting, and setting intentions before the light returns.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology reads the New Moon as the seed point of the cycle — a good time to set intentions or start something new, even if nothing visible happens yet.
psychological_interpretation: Symbolically tied to a fresh start and inward reflection before outward action — a natural pause point for deciding what to plant before the cycle of growth begins.
positive_aspects: A genuinely good, symbolically supported time to start something new, set an intention, or begin a project with a full cycle ahead of it.
challenges: Energy is low and things feel undefined — not the best time to expect visible results or push hard for immediate momentum.
career_meaning: Favorable for kicking off a new project, application, or plan, even in a small way — the visible progress comes later in the cycle.
relationship_meaning: A good time to have a quiet, intention-setting conversation about where a relationship is headed, rather than a dramatic one.
growth_meaning: An invitation to get clear on an intention before acting on it, rather than rushing into visible action prematurely.

definition: The Waxing Crescent follows the New Moon, with the Moon's illuminated sliver growing — the Sun and Moon are roughly 45 degrees apart.
traditional_interpretation: Traditionally seen as a time of tentative, building momentum — early growth that's still fragile and needs protecting rather than testing.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as the phase for taking the first concrete steps on an intention set at the New Moon — small, consistent actions rather than a big push.
psychological_interpretation: Represents early-stage commitment — the point where an idea starts becoming real through small effort, often against some initial resistance or doubt.
positive_aspects: Building momentum, early motivation, and the encouragement of visible (if small) early progress.
challenges: Doubt or impatience since results are still minor — easy to abandon an intention here if quick results are expected.
career_meaning: A good window for early-stage groundwork — research, first drafts, or initial outreach rather than a final push.
relationship_meaning: A time for small, consistent gestures that build trust, rather than expecting a big resolution all at once.
growth_meaning: Learning to trust small, unglamorous progress rather than needing immediate, visible proof that an effort is working.

definition: The First Quarter Moon occurs when the Sun and Moon are 90 degrees apart, with exactly half the Moon's face illuminated — often called the 'crisis of action' point in the lunar cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read through the lens of the square aspect it forms — a point of tension and decision that demands action rather than passive waiting.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as the point where an intention set at the New Moon meets its first real obstacle — a decision point that tests genuine commitment.
psychological_interpretation: Represents the moment friction appears and a choice has to be made — push through the obstacle or quietly let the intention go.
positive_aspects: A clarifying pressure that forces a real decision, often resulting in stronger commitment once the choice is made.
challenges: Genuine friction, obstacles, or conflict — this phase rarely feels easy, by design.
career_meaning: A good but demanding window for pushing through a stalled project or making a decision that's been avoided.
relationship_meaning: Tension in a relationship may surface here — often clarifying rather than destructive if addressed directly.
growth_meaning: Learning to treat obstacles as information about commitment rather than a sign to give up.

definition: The Waxing Gibbous follows the First Quarter, with the Moon's illuminated face growing past half — the Sun and Moon are roughly 135 degrees apart, approaching fullness.
traditional_interpretation: Traditionally read as a refining phase — the shape of the outcome is mostly visible now, and effort shifts from initiating to perfecting.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as the phase for adjustment and refinement — analyzing what's working, correcting what isn't, before the intention reaches full expression.
psychological_interpretation: Represents a build-up of anticipation and analysis — a natural, sometimes anxious phase of fine-tuning right before culmination.
positive_aspects: Clear enough progress to see what's working, with time left to make meaningful adjustments before completion.
challenges: Impatience or overanalysis — the temptation to keep tweaking indefinitely instead of letting the cycle complete.
career_meaning: A good window for revision, quality control, and final adjustments before a launch or deadline.
relationship_meaning: A time for honest evaluation of how things are going, with room to still make constructive changes.
growth_meaning: Learning to trust that enough groundwork has been laid, and that further perfectionism has diminishing returns.

definition: The Full Moon occurs when the Sun and Moon are directly opposite (180 degrees apart) and the Moon's face is fully illuminated — the culmination point of the lunar cycle, traditionally the most emotionally charged phase.
traditional_interpretation: Across many traditions the Full Moon was associated with heightened emotion, culmination, revelation, and sometimes disruption — the point where whatever has been building becomes fully visible.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology reads the Full Moon as harvest and culmination — the outcome of the intention set two weeks earlier becomes clear, for better or worse.
psychological_interpretation: A period of heightened emotional intensity and clarity — feelings and situations that have been building quietly often surface fully and demand to be acknowledged.
positive_aspects: Culmination, celebration, clarity, and the satisfaction of seeing an intention reach visible fruition.
challenges: Emotional intensity, heightened reactivity, and sometimes the surfacing of tension that had been building unnoticed.
career_meaning: A natural point for launches, presentations, or completions — results and reactions are both more visible than usual.
relationship_meaning: Emotions run high — both closeness and conflict tend to be more visible and intense during this phase.
growth_meaning: An invitation to fully acknowledge what's surfaced, rather than suppressing heightened feelings because they're inconvenient.

definition: The Waning Gibbous follows the Full Moon, with the illuminated face shrinking — the Sun and Moon are roughly 135 degrees apart on the other side of the cycle, beginning the release phase.
traditional_interpretation: Traditionally associated with gratitude and sharing the harvest — a time to distribute or teach what's been gained rather than continue pushing for more.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as a phase for reflection, gratitude, and beginning to release what's no longer needed after the Full Moon's culmination.
psychological_interpretation: Represents digestion — processing and making sense of what just culminated, before actively moving toward letting it go.
positive_aspects: Genuine insight and integration — the chance to extract real lessons from what just happened rather than rushing forward.
challenges: A dip in motivation as the cycle's peak has passed, which can feel like a letdown if mistaken for stagnation.
career_meaning: A good window for debriefs, sharing results, mentoring others, or documenting lessons learned from a recent project.
relationship_meaning: A time for processing what surfaced at the Full Moon together, with more clarity and less heat than the peak itself.
growth_meaning: Learning to sit with and extract meaning from a recent culmination rather than immediately chasing the next thing.

definition: The Last Quarter Moon occurs when the Sun and Moon are 90 degrees apart on the waning side, with exactly half the Moon's face illuminated — often called the 'crisis of consciousness' point in the lunar cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classically read through the lens of the square aspect it forms — a point of internal reckoning rather than the more outward-facing tension of the First Quarter.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as a point of releasing what's no longer serving the cycle — clearing space rather than starting anything new.
psychological_interpretation: Represents an internal reckoning — an honest look at what needs to be let go of before the cycle can complete and begin again.
positive_aspects: Clarity about what to release, and the relief that comes with actually letting go of something outdated.
challenges: Can surface old, unresolved issues that demand attention before real closure is possible.
career_meaning: A good window for closing out a project, cutting something that isn't working, or clearing a backlog before starting fresh.
relationship_meaning: A time for honest reckoning about what in a relationship needs to change or be released.
growth_meaning: Learning to release something consciously rather than carrying it forward unresolved into the next cycle.

definition: The Waning Crescent is the final phase before the next New Moon, with only a thin sliver of illumination left — the Sun and Moon are roughly 45 degrees apart on the closing side of the cycle, often called the 'balsamic' phase.
traditional_interpretation: Traditionally treated as a rest and surrender phase — a time to withdraw, reflect, and prepare rather than initiate, ahead of the coming New Moon.
modern_interpretation: Modern lunar-cycle astrology treats this as a genuine rest phase — low energy is expected and appropriate, not a problem to fix, ahead of the next cycle's fresh start.
psychological_interpretation: Represents surrender and quiet preparation — the psychological equivalent of clearing the desk before starting something genuinely new.
positive_aspects: Deep rest, honest reflection, and quiet clarity about what the next cycle should actually focus on.
challenges: Low energy and motivation that can feel discouraging if mistaken for a permanent state rather than a natural, temporary rest phase.
career_meaning: A good window for rest, reflection, and planning — not the best time to force a major new initiative before the coming New Moon.
relationship_meaning: A quiet, low-key phase best used for genuine rest together rather than pushing for a big decision or conversation.
growth_meaning: Learning to genuinely rest and let a cycle fully close, rather than forcing new momentum before it's actually time.
